🙋‍♀️ Introducing Yourself (Se Présenter)

Learn the essential phrases to tell people about yourself!

bonjour 👋

Bonjour! Je m'appelle...

Hello! My name is...

Example: Bonjour! Je m'appelle Marie. Hello! My name is Marie.
🎂
🕯️🕯️🕯️

J'ai __ ans

I am __ years old

Example: J'ai dix ans. I am 10 years old.
👤
🖐

Je suis...

I am...

👦: Je suis étudiant. I am a student - boy
👧: Je suis étudiante. I am a student - girl
🏫
📖

J'étudie à l'école...

I study at ... school

Example: J'étudie à l'école Silver Oaks I study at Silver Oaks school.
🏠
📍

J'habite à...

I live in...

Ex 1: J'habite à Paris.
Ex 2: J'habite à Hyderabad en Inde.

💡 Memory Tip:

Ils vs Elles: Use "ils" if there's even one boy in the group. Use "elles" only when the group is all girls!

🔤 Important Verbs

S'appeler (To call oneself)

Je m'appelle
Tu t'appelles
Il/Elle s'appelle
Nous nous appelons
Vous vous appelez
Ils/Elles s'appellent

Sing along to learn s'appeler!

🗣️ Dialogue : Demander et dire le nom

👤 Comment tu t'appelles ?
👦 Je m'appelle Léo !
👥 Comment il s'appelle ?
👨 Il s'appelle Paul.
👭 Elle s'appelle comment ?
👩 Elle s'appelle Sophie.

💡 Focus on "On"

What it means:

  • On = Nous (We)
  • On = we / one / people

How to conjugate:

Even though it often means "we", we conjugate it exactly like il or elle!

  • Il a = he has
  • Elle a = she has
  • On a = we have / one has

Avoir (To have)

Je ai (J'ai) (I have)
Tu as (You have)
Il/Elle/On a (He/She/One has)
Nous avons (We have)
Vous avez (You have)
Ils/Elles ont (They have)

Practice conjugating Avoir with this video!

🗣️ Dialogue : Avoir

J'ai un stylo. I have a pen.
As-tu un ordinateur ? Do you have a computer?
Il a une règle. He has a ruler.
Elle a un taille-crayon. She has a pencil sharpener.
Nous avons des livres. We have books.
Vous avez une colle ? Do you have a glue stick?
Ils ont cours de français maintenant. They have French class now.

💡 Focus: Un, Une, Des

Un - a/an or one (masculine singular).

Une - a/an or one (feminine singular).

Des - some (plural, masculine or feminine).

Être (To be)

Je suis (I am)
Tu es (You are)
Il/Elle/On est (He/She/One is)
Nous sommes (We are)
Vous êtes (You are)
Ils/Elles sont (They are)

Practice conjugating Être with this video!

Nationalities

🗣️ Dialogue : Être

👧Je suis indienne. I am Indian. (female)
👦Tu es indien ? Are you Indian? (male)
👨Il est américain. He is American.
👩Elle est américaine. She is American.
👨‍🎓👩‍🎓Nous sommes étudiants. We are students.
👫Vous êtes français ? Are you French?
👨👨Ils sont australiens. They are Australian. (male/mixed)
👩👩Elles sont japonaises. They are Japanese. (female)

📝 Regular -ER Verbs

Most French verbs end in -ER and follow the same pattern!

🔄 The -ER Pattern

Remove -ER and add these endings:

Je -e
Tu -es
Il/Elle -e
Nous -ons
Vous -ez
Ils/Elles -ent

Common -ER

Habiter (To live)

J' habite I live
Tu habites You live
Il/Elle/On habite He/She/One lives
Nous habitons We live
Vous habitez You live
Ils / Elles habitent They live

Aimer (To like)

J' aime I like
Tu aimes You like
Il/Elle/On aime He/She/One likes
Nous aimons We like
Vous aimez You like
Ils / Elles aiment They like

Parler (To speak)

Je parle I speak
Tu parles You speak
Il/Elle/On parle He/She/One speaks
Nous parlons We speak
Vous parlez You speak
Ils / Elles parlent They speak

Étudier (To study)

J' étudie I study
Tu étudies You study
Il/Elle/On étudie He/She/One studies
Nous étudions We study
Vous étudiez You study
Ils / Elles étudient They study

🌍 Culture et Civilisation : L’Identité et les Symboles de la France

(French Identity and Symbols)

Fun Fact: France is the most visited country in the world, with over 90 million tourists every year! 🏰🥖

🛑

L'Hexagone

France is often called The Hexagon because of its shape! It is the largest country in the European Union.

💶

L'Euro (€)

France uses the Euro. Before 2002, they used Francs, which were used for over 600 years!

🐓

Le Coq

The proud Rooster is the national symbol. It represents the bravery and heritage of the French people!

🎵

La Marseillaise

The national anthem is La Marseillaise. It was written in 1792 and is a song about freedom and courage!

🤝

La Devise

The motto "Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité" was born during the French Revolution over 200 years ago!

🧀

Les Fromages

France makes over 1,600 types of cheese! Some people say there's a different cheese for every day of the year.

🥐🥖

Les Pâtisseries et Le Pain

The Baguette is so important that its recipe is protected by law! French people buy it fresh every morning.

🐌

Les Escargots

Snails are a famous delicacy. French people eat around 30,000 tons of snails every single year!

🍷

Le Vin

France is one of the world's top wine producers. Wine making has been part of French culture for over 2,000 years!

👗✨

La Mode & Les Parfums

Paris is the fashion capital! They make beautiful clothes and the best smelling perfumes!

🚴‍♂️

Le Tour de France

The most prestigious bicycle race in the world! It lasts 3 weeks and travels across mountains and through tiny villages.

🇫🇷

Le Drapeau Français

The French flag is called the Tricolore. Its colors are Blue, White, and Red (Bleu, Blanc, Rouge)!

🎬✨

Le Festival de Cannes

One of the most famous film festivals in the world! Movie stars from all over come to the French Riviera to celebrate cinema.

😘

La Bise

French people often greet friends by kissing on the cheeks! This is called "La Bise". The number of kisses changes depending on the city!
